question: An infinitely long solid non-conducting cylinder of radius $R$ has a uniform volume charge density $+ρ$. The axis of the cylinder is the z-axis. A thin, infinite line charge with a uniform linear density $-λ$ is placed parallel to the cylinder's axis, passing through the point $(R/2, 0, 0)$. The system is constructed such that the net charge per unit length of the cylinder is equal in magnitude to the linear charge density of the line, i.e., $ρπR² = λ$. What is the magnitude of the net electric field at the point $(R, 0, 0)$ on the surface of the cylinder?
